title: What Is Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery? knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes What Is Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery??
options: Continuous integration validates changes frequently; continuous delivery keeps validated changes ready to release; continuous deployment automatically releases qualifying changes.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: Continuous integration validates changes frequently; continuous delivery keeps validated changes ready to release; continuous deployment automatically releases qualifying changes.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of what is continuous integration and continuous delivery?: Continuous integration validates changes frequently; continuous delivery keeps validated changes ready to release; continuous deployment automatically releases qualifying changes. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “Continuous integration (CI)”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Use a scoped token, validate request inputs and event payloads, check HTTP/error status, handle pagination and rate limits, and avoid logging credentials or unneeded private response data.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
questions.answer_key: Use a scoped token, validate request inputs and event payloads, check HTTP/error status, handle pagination and rate limits, and avoid logging credentials or unneeded private response data.
questions.explanation: Continuous integration (CI): Use a scoped token, validate request inputs and event payloads, check HTTP/error status, handle pagination and rate limits, and avoid logging credentials or unneeded private response data. questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to what is continuous integration and continuous delivery??
options: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Continuous integration validates changes frequently; continuous delivery keeps validated changes ready to release; continuous deployment automatically releases qualifying changes. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
